utterance:
Graham, here's exactly what's going on and what I'm doing, so there are no surprises.

WHAT IT IS: Your heart tracing shows a heart attack — an artery supplying the lower part of your heart is blocked. This isn't indigestion, and the Quick-Eze not working fits that. The tightness you felt climbing ladders this past week was your heart giving you warnings. You did the right thing coming in, and your wife was right to insist.

WHAT I'VE ALREADY DONE: I've called 000 and an ambulance is on the way now. I've phoned the emergency department and given them a handover with your tracing, so the team who can open the artery are expecting you. I've given you 300 mg of aspirin to chew, plus a second blood-thinning tablet (ticagrelor) — together these help stop the clot getting bigger.

WHAT I HAVE DELIBERATELY NOT GIVEN YOU: the usual under-the-tongue angina spray (GTN). Because you took Viagra last night, that spray could drop your blood pressure dangerously, and your pressure is already on the low side at 104/68 with a slow pulse of 54. I've told the hospital team about the tablet so they don't give it to you either — that's the only reason I've mentioned it, and it stays otherwise confidential. Your oxygen level is normal at 96%, so you don't need oxygen either.

WHILE WE WAIT: Stay sitting back in the chair and don't get up or walk around — I'll keep checking your pulse and blood pressure every few minutes, and we have a defibrillator right here if your heart rhythm misbehaves. Don't eat or drink anything, in case you need a procedure. And under no circumstances drive yourself anywhere.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: The ambulance will take you to a hospital that can do an angiogram and usually put in a small stent to open the blocked artery — the sooner that's done, the more heart muscle is saved, which is why we're moving fast.

AFTERWARDS: Your blood pressure tablet will be held today and the hospital will sort out your medicines; you'll stay on your cholesterol tablet and be given others to protect your heart. And stopping smoking is the single most powerful thing you can do to keep this from happening again — we'll set up support for that when you're recovering.

If the pain gets worse, you feel more breathless, more sick, more dizzy or like you might pass out — tell me straight away, don't wait to be polite.
